subject.title: FRD: first-class multi-tenant RBAC (tenant claim on session/run/approval + tenant-scoped operator scopes + tenant-aware audit + fail-closed defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt hostile same-gateway tenant isolation as a core security boundary, or keep mutually untrusted tenants outside one Gateway boundary?
rationale: Current docs deliberately disclaim that boundary, and the request changes auth semantics, stored state, approval validity, audit meaning, and fail-closed defaults.

options.title: Keep open and decide the threat model
options.body: Treat this FRD as the canonical security/product decision point, then decompose only the accepted boundary into smaller implementation issues.

options.title: Reject core tenancy
options.body: Close the FRD with a clear statement that downstream platforms must enforce tenant isolation above OpenClaw or by running separate Gateways.

options.title: Narrow to tool-policy work
options.body: Decline the full tenant boundary for now and route only the operator-scope-to-tool-policy slice to the narrower open RFC.

recommendation.title: Keep open and decide the threat model
recommendation.body: Treat this FRD as the canonical security/product decision point, then decompose only the accepted boundary into smaller implementation issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The best available history signal is prior authorship of the Gateway trust-boundary and multi-user security guidance this FRD would change.
